clue.text: Pop CD's sales stats? Disappointing if in these

definitions.meaning: the sales numbers for pop singles, the figures for single releases
a score or tally below ten, a let-down for a chart act

explanation.surface: A music critic muses on poor chart returns for a pop record.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it is the chart numbers for singles; as an idiom it means any count under ten, which is a poor result.

clue.text: Product of St Trinians, head abandoned on the way

indicators.note: a product is something made from raw material, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement
the opening letter of the words St Trinians is dropped

explanation.surface: A pupil of the fictional unruly girls' school wanders off along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head abandoned' drops the S of ST TRINIANS, leaving TTRINIANS, which 'Product of' rearranges. St Trinian's is a fictional British school famous for anarchic schoolgirls.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or people in transit are travelling, still en route to their destination.

clue.text: Brotherly name, hard and masculine

parts.note: grim means harsh, hard to bear

explanation.surface: A family name is described as tough and manly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brothers Grimm collected German fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimm is the surname shared by Jacob and Wilhelm, the famous fairy-tale brothers.

clue.text: PM with unfinished story of toothless creatures

parts.note: Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister in the 1950s

indicators.note: the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister tells a half-told tale about animals without teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony EDEN was UK Prime Minister 1955-57; 'unfinished' cuts the last E from TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate animals such as sloths and anteaters lack teeth, and this adjective relates to them.

clue.text: Dressed for cycling almost? Not what you'd expect a rambler to say

definitions.text: Not what you'd expect a rambler to say

indicators.note: the phrase is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: cyclists often ride wearing shorts, so they are in shorts

explanation.surface: A walker kitted out like a cyclist says something unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambler' looks like a country walker in cycling gear, but here it means a long-winded talker, who would never say 'briefly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means briefly or to sum up, the opposite of what a talker who rambles on would say.

clue.text: As one international body wants nothing to interrupt hostility

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: the zero breaks into the middle of the word for hostility

parts.note: animus means ill will or hostility
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The United Nations wants peace, nothing breaking into the enmity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As one' looks like a link phrase but is the definition; 'to interrupt' signals the zero breaking into the hostility word.
explanation.definitionFit: A unanimous decision is one where everyone acts together, in complete agreement.

clue.text: Be patronising to women with no leader

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: sexist describes condescension or prejudice towards women

explanation.surface: A plea not to talk down to women, with nobody in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no leader' drops the S from SEXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To be and to exist are synonyms: both mean to have being.

clue.text: Like the Pope's topping, moving world reception (when ring lost)

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order
the ring letter is taken out of the fodder

parts.note: O is a ring, from its shape

explanation.surface: A papal headpiece gets a global welcome, though a ring goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes one O (ring) from WORLD RECEPTION; 'moving' rearranges the remaining thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal tiara has three tiers of crowns, so it is described as having a threefold crown.

clue.text: March is in this requiem Dal put out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mournful requiem by a composer called Dal is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is not the month: a military march is written in four beats to the bar. 'out' rearranges REQUIEM DAL PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Marches are typically in a metre of four beats per bar, which musicians call this time signature.

clue.text: Touchy feeling exhibited by Grahame's character

definitions.meaning: the quality of Ratty, the water rat in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A character in a children's novel displays prickliness.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is the river-loving water rat in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, so his quality is playfully named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British for irritable, so the noun means irritability; it also names the trait of Grahame's Ratty.

clue.text: TV reporter, once the centre of fun for so long

parts.note: Kate Adie is a former BBC television news correspondent

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word fun is taken

explanation.surface: A former TV journalist is the life and soul of the party for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate ADIE was a famous BBC war correspondent; 'the centre of' fun gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'so long' is a farewell, and this French word is a goodbye too.

clue.text: Holy work, taking the source of sin in hand

indicators.note: the hand word takes in the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: the palm is the inside of the hand

indicators.note: the first letter of the word sin is taken

explanation.surface: A sacred text is held in the hand, despite its origins in sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts S (source of sin) inside PALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, as in the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Clumsy oaf, heartless and warped externally

indicators.note: the warped word sits outside, around the other letters

parts.note: twisted means warped or bent out of shape

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word oaf is removed

explanation.surface: A bumbling oaf is described as cruel and bent inside and out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy oaf' reads as one phrase, but 'Clumsy' alone is the definition and 'oaf' is the fodder that 'heartless' cuts; 'externally' wraps the warped word round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with two fists and no finesse is awkward, so this adjective means clumsy or crude.

clue.text: Calm sea ruffled by spilt fuel

indicators.note: ruffled water is disturbed, so these letters are mixed up
spilt suggests scattering, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A tranquil sea is disturbed by an oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffled' turns SEA into EAS, and 'spilt' turns FUEL into EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Easeful is a literary word meaning restful or peaceful, giving ease.

clue.text: Spider has Lew quaking with nun during a month

indicators.note: the shaken letters fall during, inside, the month word

parts.note: Feb is the abbreviation for February

indicators.note: quaking means shaking, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A man called Lew trembles alongside a nun when a spider appears one month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaking' shakes up the two names together, and 'during' sets the result inside the month after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The funnel-web is a venomous Australian spider named after its funnel-shaped web.

clue.text: Philosopher turned author, accepting Sartre finally

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in another letter
turned means changed around, so these letters are rearranged
the last letter of the name Sartre is taken

explanation.surface: A thinker becomes a writer and embraces Sartre's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges AUTHOR, and 'accepting' adds E (Sartre finally) inside. Sartre, a philosopher himself, tempts as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was an American philosopher and essayist, author of Walden.

clue.text: Conductor gets to choose bar and key

parts.note: to elect is to choose
a rod is a bar
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An orchestral conductor gets to pick a bar and a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra, but here it is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is an electrical conductor through which current enters or leaves.

clue.text: True about metal being of light-sensitive tissue

indicators.note: the word for true goes around the metal

parts.note: real means genuine, true
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A true story about metal and tissue that responds to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True' is the container word here, not part of the definition; 'about' signals it goes round the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, and this adjective relates to it.

clue.text: Pleasing as a lollipop that's calorie-free

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so that letter goes

parts.note: a lollipop is meant to be licked, so it is lickable
C is an abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: A diet lollipop is described as tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: '-free' removes C (calorie) from LICKABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Likable means pleasant and easy to like, so pleasing is a synonym.

clue.text: High points before spring surge

indicators.note: the first piece goes before the second

parts.note: ups are good times, as in ups and downs
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Peaks come before a spring surge of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To upswell is to rise up or surge, as water does from a source.

clue.text: Experience less than life

parts.note: under means below, less than
go means energy or vitality, liveliness

explanation.surface: Experience counts for less than living itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo is to experience or endure something.

clue.text: Deny wreck twisted head to one side

indicators.note: twisted means bent into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denies a car crash left them with a cricked neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges DENY WRECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wry-necked means having the neck twisted so the head tilts to one side, as in torticollis.

clue.text: Rough, old b-boy, retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a b-boy is a breakdancer, taken as written

explanation.surface: An old breakdancer hangs up his dancing shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses OBBOY. A YOBBO is British slang for a loutish young man, a rough.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a hooligan, the same as a yob or lout.

clue.text: Choral work: "The first word in champagne?" About time!

indicators.note: the champagne name goes about, around the other letter

parts.note: Moet is the first word of the champagne house Moet et Chandon

explanation.surface: Someone at a party shouts for champagne, complaining it has taken long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' places T inside MOET.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition.

clue.text: Society member, as in "servant"

indicators.note: the word for as goes in the servant word

parts.note: a man is a manservant
so can mean as, in the sense of thus

explanation.surface: A member of a club is described as a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: A MASON is a Freemason, member of a fraternal society.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mason is a member of the Freemasons, a secretive fraternal society.

clue.text: Joint from which non-British totter back

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read backwards
B, the abbreviation for British, is removed

parts.note: to wobble is to totter

explanation.surface: A joint from which foreigners stagger home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-British' drops one B from WOBBLE, leaving WOBLE, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the joint between the upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Give a superlative performance using rod and poles — to empty space!

parts.note: a bar is a rod
N and S are the north and south poles
taken as written

indicators.note: the word for space is emptied of its inner letters

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A stunning show using rods and poles in an empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' takes the middle out of ROOM, leaving RM.
explanation.definitionFit: To barnstorm is to tour giving rousing performances, or to perform with great flair.

clue.text: Generous whisky bar? Journalist added "very flexible"

parts.note: a double is a two-measure serving of spirits
a joint is an informal word for a bar or club
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist describes a large whisky in a bar as very bendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-jointed people have unusually flexible joints.
